nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{end}_1, \mathrm{end}_2 : E \to V$ be maps, viewed as an undirected multigraph on $V$ in which each edge $e \in E$ has endpoints $\mathrm{end}_1(e)$ and $\mathrm{end}_2(e)$. For a finite set $F \subseteq E$, vertices $u, v \in V$ are adjacent using $F$ when some $e \in F$ has $\mathrm{end}_1(e) = u$ and $\mathrm{end}_2(e) = v$, or $\mathrm{end}_1(e) = v$ and $\mathrm{end}_2(e) = u$.
nodes.title: Adjacency through an edge set

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite set and $\mathrm{end}_1, \mathrm{end}_2 : E \to V$ be maps, viewed as an undirected multigraph on $V$ in which each edge $e \in E$ has endpoints $\mathrm{end}_1(e)$ and $\mathrm{end}_2(e)$. For a finite set $X \subseteq V$, the cut of $X$ is the set of edges $e \in E$ such that exactly one of $\mathrm{end}_1(e)$ and $\mathrm{end}_2(e)$ lies in $X$. Loops never cross a cut.
nodes.title: Cut of a vertex set

nodes.title: Degree counts incident edges in a loopless edge set

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{end}_1, \mathrm{end}_2 : E \to V$ be maps, viewed as an undirected multigraph on $V$ in which each edge $e \in E$ has endpoints $\mathrm{end}_1(e)$ and $\mathrm{end}_2(e)$. nodes.title: Degree within an edge set

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{end}_1, \mathrm{end}_2 : E \to V$ be maps, viewed as an undirected multigraph on $V$ in which each edge $e \in E$ has endpoints $\mathrm{end}_1(e)$ and $\mathrm{end}_2(e)$. For a vertex $v \in V$ and a finite set $F \subseteq E$, the edges of $F$ incident to $v$ form the finite set of all $e \in F$ with $\mathrm{end}_1(e) = v$ or $\mathrm{end}_2(e) = v$. An edge appears once even when it is a loop.
nodes.title: Edges incident to a vertex

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{end}_1, \mathrm{end}_2 : E \to V$ be maps, viewed as an undirected multigraph on $V$ in which each edge $e \in E$ has endpoints $\mathrm{end}_1(e)$ and $\mathrm{end}_2(e)$. nodes.title: Edge sets connected on their support

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{end}_1, \mathrm{end}_2 : E \to V$ be maps, viewed as an undirected multigraph on $V$ in which each edge $e \in E$ has endpoints $\mathrm{end}_1(e)$ and $\mathrm{end}_2(e)$. The support of a finite set $F \subseteq E$ is the set of vertices $v \in V$ such that $\mathrm{end}_1(e) = v$ or $\mathrm{end}_2(e) = v$ for some $e \in F$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
